name: Sea-to-Sky Highway
description: Vancouver to Whistler and Pemberton along Howe Sound, past Shannon Falls and the Stawamus Chief, climbing into the Coast Mountains

name: Duffey Lake Road
description: Highway 99 beyond Pemberton to Lillooet: steep grades, tight switchbacks and glacier-fed Duffey Lake, a favourite loop for Vancouver drivers

name: Fraser Canyon Highway
description: The Trans-Canada from Hope through the Fraser Canyon to Cache Creek, through tunnels above the river and past Hell's Gate

name: Crowsnest Highway
description: Hope through Manning Park, the Similkameen and Osoyoos wine country, with mountain passes and desert valleys

name: Okanagan Highway
description: Through the Okanagan Valley from Osoyoos past Penticton and Kelowna to Vernon, along lakes, orchards and vineyards

name: Pacific Rim Highway
description: Across Vancouver Island from Parksville past Cathedral Grove and Kennedy Lake to Tofino and Ucluelet

name: Banff-Windermere Highway
description: From Castle Junction over Vermilion Pass through Kootenay National Park to Radium Hot Springs and the Sinclair Canyon

name: Icefields Parkway
description: Lake Louise to Jasper along the Continental Divide past Bow Lake, Peyto Lake and the Columbia Icefield, one of the world's great drives

name: Bow Valley Parkway
description: Slower, wildlife-rich alternative to the Trans-Canada between Banff and Lake Louise, past Johnston Canyon

name: Highwood Pass (Kananaskis Trail)
description: Through Kananaskis Country over Highwood Pass, Canada's highest paved pass; the summit section is closed December to mid-June

name: Cowboy Trail
description: Foothills ranch country west of Calgary along the Rockies, through Longview, Black Diamond and Turner Valley

name: Niagara Parkway
description: Along the Niagara River from Fort Erie past the Falls to Niagara-on-the-Lake, through parkland and wine country

name: Highway 60 through Algonquin
description: The Parkway Corridor across Algonquin Provincial Park, lakes and forest with moose sightings and famous fall colour

name: Bruce Peninsula Highway
description: Up the Bruce Peninsula to Tobermory, between Georgian Bay cliffs and Lake Huron beaches

name: Thousand Islands Parkway
description: Along the St. Lawrence River between Gananoque and Brockville, past the Thousand Islands

name: Muskoka Highway 118
description: Winding cottage-country road through Muskoka and Haliburton lakes and Canadian Shield rock cuts

name: Gaspé Peninsula (Route 132)
description: The loop around the Gaspé Peninsula along the St. Lawrence, past seaside villages, Forillon and Percé Rock

name: Route 362 in Charlevoix
description: Rollercoaster coast road from Baie-Saint-Paul to La Malbaie high above the St. Lawrence

name: Chemin du Roy
description: Canada's oldest road, along the north shore of the St. Lawrence from Montreal to Quebec City through historic villages

name: Saguenay Fjord (Route 170)
description: Along the south side of the Saguenay Fjord, with lookouts over the cliffs and the fjord villages

name: Route des Baleines (Côte-Nord)
description: Route 138 from Tadoussac along the North Shore of the St. Lawrence estuary, with whale watching at Tadoussac and Les Bergeronnes

name: Kootenay Lake (Highway 3A)
description: Creston up the east shore of Kootenay Lake, across on the free Kootenay Lake ferry, and on to Nelson

name: Malahat Drive
description: The Trans-Canada's climb over the Malahat north of Victoria, with lookouts over Saanich Inlet

name: David Thompson Highway
description: Saskatchewan River Crossing to Nordegg past turquoise Abraham Lake, the quiet back door into the Rockies

name: Dinosaur Trail
description: Loop through the Red Deer River badlands around Drumheller, with the Bleriot Ferry and Horsethief Canyon

name: Waterton Lakes (Highway 6 and the Akamina Parkway)
description: Where the prairie meets the mountains: Highway 6 from Pincher Creek into Waterton Lakes National Park

name: Lake Superior Coast (Highway 17)
description: Sault Ste. Marie to Wawa through Lake Superior Provincial Park, past Agawa Bay and the Montreal River hill

name: Loyalist Parkway
description: Along Lake Ontario from Trenton through Prince Edward County to Kingston, with the Glenora ferry

name: Georgian Bay and Blue Mountains (Highway 26)
description: Along Georgian Bay from Wasaga Beach through Collingwood and the Blue Mountains to Meaford

name: Cabot Trail
description: Loop around Cape Breton Island's highlands and coast, through Cape Breton Highlands National Park and Acadian and Gaelic villages

name: Lighthouse Route (Peggy's Cove and Lunenburg)
description: South Shore from Halifax past Peggy's Cove, Mahone Bay and Lunenburg to Yarmouth, fishing villages and lighthouses all the way

name: Peggy's Cove Road
description: Short loop from Halifax over granite barrens to the lighthouse at Peggy's Cove

name: Fundy Coastal Drive (Route 114)
description: Through Fundy National Park to Alma and the Hopewell Rocks, on the shore of the world's highest tides

name: Fundy Trail Parkway
description: Clifftop parkway east of St. Martins along the Bay of Fundy with lookouts and suspension bridges

name: Central Coastal Drive (Green Gables Shore)
description: Red cliffs, beaches and Cavendish along Prince Edward Island's north shore and the national park

name: Viking Trail
description: Deer Lake through Gros Morne National Park and up the Northern Peninsula to L'Anse aux Meadows, the Viking site

name: Irish Loop
description: Around the southern Avalon Peninsula from St. John's past Witless Bay's puffins and whales and Ferryland

name: Qu'Appelle Valley
description: Down off the prairie into the valley of the Fishing Lakes around Fort Qu'Appelle and Katepwa, rolling hills in a flat province

name: Cypress Hills
description: Pine-covered hills rising out of the prairie, with the Gap Road between the Saskatchewan and Alberta parks

name: Grasslands Ecotour Scenic Drive
description: Gravel drive through the Frenchman River valley in Grasslands National Park, with bison and prairie dog towns

name: Prince Albert National Park (Highway 263)
description: Winding boreal forest road into Prince Albert National Park and Waskesiu Lake

name: Riding Mountain National Park (Highway 10)
description: Up the Manitoba Escarpment and across Riding Mountain through Wasagaming on Clear Lake

name: Whiteshell Provincial Park (Road 307)
description: Canadian Shield lakes, rock and forest east of Winnipeg, past Rainbow Falls and Seven Sisters Falls
